chunks: "I'll take the RC low-pass as the example, with a corner frequency f c equals 1 over (2 pi RC) , say 1 kilohertz. I draw two stacked plots with a log frequency axis.
On the magnitude plot, in dB, the response is flat at 0 decibels well below the corner, because the capacitor is basically open. At the corner it's down 3 decibels, that's 0.
707 of the input. Above the corner it falls along a straight line at minus 20 decibels per decade, so 20 decibels down at 10 kilohertz, 40 decibels down at 100 kilohertz.
On the straight-line sketch I put the corner where the two asymptotes meet, and the true curve sits 3 decibels under that point.
On the phase plot, it starts at 0 degrees at low frequency, passes through minus 45 degrees exactly at the corner, and goes toward minus 90 at high frequency.
It's about minus 6 degrees one decade below the corner and minus 84 one decade above.
If it's a high-pass, I mirror it: the magnitude rises at plus 20 decibels per decade up to the corner then is flat, and the phase goes from plus 90 down to zero, plus 45 at the corner.
Same corner, same minus 3 decibels point."
